description: Availability commitments are broken by capacity limits reached without warning. Monitoring demand against capacity is what turns a future outage into a planned expansion.
implementation_guidance:
Monitor utilization of compute, storage, database connections, quotas and rate limits.
Set alert thresholds below the point of failure, leaving time to act.
Use autoscaling where the workload supports it, and test that it engages under load.
Review capacity trends and provider quotas periodically against forecast growth.
name: Capacity management

evidence.name: Capacity review
Capacity actions that were taken

description: Backups are the last defence against ransomware, accidental deletion and regional failure. Automation removes reliance on anyone remembering to run them, and monitoring ensures a silent failure is not discovered during an incident.
implementation_guidance:
Enable automated backups on every production data store, with frequency and retention aligned to the documented RPO.
Encrypt backups at rest and restrict restore permissions to a small, reviewed group.
Alert on backup failure and on jobs that have not completed within the expected window.
Keep at least one copy in a separate region or account, so a single compromise cannot destroy both data and backups.
name: Automated, monitored backups

evidence.name: Backup policy covering scope, frequency and retention
Backup failure alerts and follow up

description: A backup that has never been restored is an assumption, not a control. Restore testing is what converts it into a demonstrated recovery capability and surfaces the gaps before they matter.
implementation_guidance:
Perform a full restore test at least annually, and after significant changes to the data platform.
Restore into an isolated environment and validate data completeness and integrity, not just job success.
Measure actual restore time against the documented RTO and RPO.
Record the test date, scope, result and any corrective actions.
name: Backup restore testing

evidence.name: Restore test plan and results
Measured recovery time against the target

description: Third-party risk cannot be managed against an unknown population. The vendor register is the base list that due diligence, agreements and access reviews all work from.
implementation_guidance:
Maintain a vendor register with owner, service provided, criticality and the data each vendor can access.
Reconcile it against accounts payable and identity-provider records to find unregistered vendors.
Record contract dates and renewal points so review happens before commitments auto-renew.
Review the register at least annually and remove vendors no longer in use, confirming their access is revoked.
name: Vendor inventory

evidence.name: Vendor inventory with owner, data and criticality

description: Vendors inherit the data entrusted to you, and their weaknesses become yours. Diligence scaled to risk is what makes that inheritance a decision rather than an accident.
implementation_guidance:
Assess vendor security before granting access to systems or data, with depth scaled to criticality.
Obtain and review a SOC 2 report or equivalent for critical vendors, reading the exceptions and complementary user entity controls rather than filing the report unread.
Re-review critical vendors at least annually and on material change.
Record the assessment, the decision and any accepted risk.
name: Vendor security due diligence

evidence.name: Security assessment for each critical vendor
Vendor assurance reports that were reviewed such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001

description: Software adopted outside procurement still processes company data, but without a vendor review, a data processing agreement or an offboarding path. Detection is what brings it back under management.
implementation_guidance:
Monitor identity-provider sign-ins and OAuth grants to detect newly adopted applications.
Review expense and card data for software purchases made outside procurement.
Route detected applications into the vendor onboarding process, or remove access.
Make the approved request path easy enough that informal adoption is not the path of least resistance.
name: Shadow-IT detection

evidence.name: Review of newly discovered applications
Decision to approve or remove each one

description: Subprocessors receiving customer or personal data extend the trust boundary. Customer contracts and privacy regimes commonly require that they are disclosed and, in many cases, that customers are notified before new ones are added.
implementation_guidance:
Maintain a subprocessor list recording the entity, purpose, data categories and location.
Publish it where customer commitments require, and keep the published version current.
Reconcile the list against vendors that actually receive data, using the data map.
Follow the contractual notice process before adding a subprocessor.
name: Subprocessor management

evidence.name: Subprocessor list shared with customers
Notices to customers of subprocessor changes

description: Where infrastructure runs in a cloud provider, physical security is performed by that provider and carved out of your audit. Reviewing their report is what makes that reliance a verified control rather than an assumption.
implementation_guidance:
Obtain the provider's current SOC 2 or ISO 27001 report at least annually.
Review the exceptions and the complementary user entity controls, and confirm you operate the controls the provider expects of you.
Disclose the subservice organization and the carve-out in the system description.
Record the review, the reviewer and any issues identified.
name: Cloud physical security (subservice review)

evidence.name: Cloud provider assurance report that was reviewed such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001
Review of the carve out and the controls the entity must add

description: Offices still hold laptops, printed material and network access. Where an office is in scope, physical access control is what stops digital controls from being bypassed by simply walking in.
implementation_guidance:
Control office entry with badge or equivalent access, and restrict server or network areas further.
Maintain a visitor log and require visitors to be escorted in sensitive areas.
Revoke badges as part of offboarding, and reconcile active badges against active staff periodically.
Retain access records for a defined period, and secure printed confidential material and disposal.
name: Office physical access controls

evidence.name: Physical access policy for offices
Access list and badge records
Visitor log
